summary_paragraph: A 58-year-old woman with HCV- and alcohol-related cirrhosis, hepatocellular carcinoma, and type 2 diabetes was admitted due to confusion caused by hepatic encephalopathy. The episode was triggered by inconsistent lactulose use and recent intake of oxycodone and zolpidem (Ambien), both of which are metabolized by the liver and can worsen mental status in cirrhosis. She improved with frequent lactulose dosing, discontinuation of zolpidem, and reduction of oxycodone. Her mental status cleared by hospital day 2, and asterixis resolved. Imaging showed no new liver lesions or ascites. A first-degree burn on her forearm, sustained while cooking, was managed with wound care. Asymptomatic bacteriuria was noted but not treated. She was discharged home with a visiting nurse, instructions to adhere to lactulose, a plan to taper oxycodone, and follow-up with her primary and liver specialists.
